chapter: Opinions on singers, promotion and originality
title: Electronics covering up lack of quality
summary: Edison and Dance complain that records and amplification hide poor musicians.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: : I mean, there are very funny things. I mean, you take B. B. King, who was doing pretty well. If you hear him in person, he has a great little band, sounds great. But the records they make are terrible. You know, they're all hammed up, the material is rough.

Well, that's it. They take all the equipment and put behind somebody who doesn't have the quality and make them sound good. But they won't take the equipment and things that they need to put behind somebody that's already good to make them sound better, you know.

You know, you can take these rock and roll musicians, they've got equipment -- you've never seen the equipment they have around them to make them sound good, you know. That's what I don't like about the electronics. I think that's the worst thing that ever happened, I really do. When you have to use electronics, to me it covers up the quality that you don't have. If you've got quality, why should you have something electric to make it come over, you know. If you've got quality, you don't need something to make you sound good. And you take some of this electronics away from these musicians nowadays, it would be absolutely horrible to listen to. It would be terrible.
